chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ayesha said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'The people of Barirah stipulated their guardianship (walayah).' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The guardianship is for the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah (a specific slave woman mentioned in the context)
key_terms.وَلَاء: Guardianship / Right of kinship that follows emancipation

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling regarding the guardianship (walayah) of an emancipated slave in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-walā’ li-man a‘taq' (guardianship belongs to the emancipator), illustrating how the Prophet (peace be upon him) upheld the contractual rights of Barirah’s masters even when they stipulated it. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is foundational for understanding the legal ties of manumission, distinguishing between the spiritual freedom of the slave and the material rights retained by the former master. The incident highlights the Prophet’s adherence to established social contracts, reinforcing the concept that emancipation creates a permanent legal bond unless explicitly waived.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ayesha said to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘The people of Bareyra are stipulating their guardianship’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The guardianship is for the one who emancipates’.
